nodes.title: Crystal — implementation manifest
nodes.summary: Machine-readable Crystal implementation checkpoint describing implemented boundaries, Reader Core slices, test/CI evidence, and explicit runtime non-authorizations; the file is dated and does not replace live GitHub or CURRENT_STATE.
nodes.why_read: Open when a machine reader needs a structured inventory of what Crystal components and boundaries were implemented at the recorded checkpoint; reconcile volatile state against live GitHub and docs/ai/CURRENT_STATE.md.

nodes.title: Crystal — CanonicalView / Trusted-Only Read Mode RFC
nodes.summary: Read-path Canon projection contract. Strict answer-grounding is partially implemented; review/full_graph modes, per-fact trace replayability, and conflicting-VERIFIED surfacing/abstention remain unimplemented.
nodes.why_read: Open when distinguishing physical L3 membership from strict Canon grounding or when assessing the still-open read-mode/conflict-handling remainder.

research.research_question: How should Crystal expose a strict trusted-only read projection without changing L3 storage or TruthGate write authority?
prior_evidence: Strict CanonicalView grounding is wired into answer generation.
Physical L3 contains multiple truth/epistemic states.
results: CONTEXTUAL exists as pure tested function but is not default-wired.
limitations: trace replayability not independently reverified per fact
conflicting VERIFIED facts policy still open

nodes.title: Crystal — Reader Core RC-0 Architecture Contract
nodes.summary: Research architecture for attentive, source-grounded long-document reading upstream of epistemic admission, with explicit coverage, multi-pass reading, source fidelity, contradiction candidates, and provenance boundaries.
nodes.why_read: Open when evaluating long-document reading, coverage/re-read semantics, source-linked reader artifacts, or whether a proposed reading mechanism would bypass Crystal admission boundaries.

research.research_question: What minimum auditable reading layer can preserve source fidelity and coverage without becoming a second truth authority?
competing_hypotheses: explicit multi-pass source-linked reading state is useful
limitations: architecture contract is not a dedicated runtime

nodes.title: Crystal — Contradiction Policy
nodes.summary: Implemented baseline for pending WORLD_FACT contradiction review: high-precision advisory detection, immutable reports, fail-closed normal approval, explicit curator dispositions, and no automatic epistemic winner.
nodes.why_read: Open when a contradiction candidate reaches review or when checking why similarity, confidence, recency, or source count cannot automatically choose a winner.

nodes.title: Titan — Execution Observation & Evaluation Contract
nodes.summary: R1 proposed research contract for read-only execution trace/span projection and bounded evaluation, explicitly separating observation from causation, evidence use, Canon, belief, policy, and action authority.
nodes.why_read: Open when designing execution observability/evaluation or importing tracing ideas; it defines the non-authority ceiling and the failure→fixture path without admitting a new runtime owner.

research.research_question: Can Titan expose a bounded execution tree and evaluation path without inventing causation or acquiring truth/policy authority?
prior_evidence: Titan already distinguishes retrieved/serialized/transmitted from demonstrably used and answer-supporting evidence.
Operational history reconstruction is incomplete as a first-class persisted execution tree.

nodes.title: Titan — Research Intake Protocol
nodes.summary: Research-governance contract for classifying ENGINEERING_NOW, RESEARCH_CANDIDATE, PARKED, REJECTED, and SUPERSEDED ideas while preserving cross-project ownership and evidence-based promotion.
nodes.why_read: Open when a new donor idea, audit finding, external pattern, or cross-project proposal appears and needs routing without becoming accepted architecture by implication.

nodes.title: Titan — Known Risks and Required Proof
nodes.summary: Current risk register separating closed/reduced risks from still-open proof and governance gaps, including no current Operator GO, bounded Continuity evidence, solo-governance limits, and non-universal erasure/concurrency claims.
nodes.why_read: Open after Titan current state when evaluating a proposed implementation or promotion against the live risk/proof boundary; recheck volatile issue/PR lifecycle in GitHub.

nodes.title: Titan — Evaluation Replay Protocol
nodes.summary: Proposed offline deterministic evaluation contract over fixed corpora, questions, policy/configuration, immutable receipts, and bounded candidate forks; it measures change without controlling production routing or Canon.
nodes.why_read: Open when comparing Titan configurations or converting a bounded failure into reproducible evaluation evidence while preserving immutable package identities and critical-failure visibility.

nodes.title: Native Kernel — project-state.json
nodes.summary: Machine-readable project-state overlay for research/laboratory tracks, architecture refoundation, BPV1 evidence lineage, residual A10 validation, H11 admission state, and explicit production/runtime freezes; live HEAD is intentionally resolved from GitHub.
nodes.why_read: Open alongside docs/ai/CURRENT_STATE.md for deterministic current machine fields and gate lineage; do not treat historical checkpoint literals inside the snapshot as the live GitHub HEAD.

nodes.title: Native Kernel — Known Risks and Required Proof
nodes.summary: Active-risk register retaining the current H11 independence/admission blocker, provisional formal-authority interpretation, production-overclaim risks, bounded evidence limitations, and historical/current-state separation.
nodes.why_read: Open when assessing whether a new result actually closes Native Kernel evidence/authority gaps; it explicitly blocks self-certification, historical/current collapse, and production overclaim.

nodes.title: Native Kernel — Architecture Re-foundation
nodes.summary: Blueprint-before-runtime architecture program separating technology-neutral semantic obligations from the bounded Python/PostgreSQL/SQLite reference laboratory and preserving provisional status after independent challenge/reconciliation.
nodes.why_read: Open for the A1–A10 blueprint lineage and the problem-level candidate minimum; use current-state surfaces for the present gate because historical NEXT markers remain preserved inside this document.

nodes.title: Native Kernel — BPV1 D7 Integrated Re-review
nodes.summary: Historical integrated re-review concluding that selected semantic obligations were strengthened for one bounded conventional-digital cross-lineage realization while six A10 hypotheses remained not tested and Final Canon/runtime thaw stayed unauthorized.
nodes.why_read: Open to understand why the provisional architecture was strengthened after BPV1 without universalizing the result; current routing must continue through CURRENT_STATE/project-state.

nodes.title: Mentaury Soul — project_state.json
nodes.summary: Derived machine snapshot of Soul V1 research-core completion, implemented bounded components, and explicit non-authorized action/retrieval/tool/identity/relationship/runtime capabilities; live GitHub and CURRENT_STATUS override conflicts.
nodes.why_read: Open for a compact machine-readable Soul snapshot, then resolve live GitHub and docs/CURRENT_STATUS.md before using volatile fields.

nodes.title: Mentaury Soul — Cognitive Orientation View v0.1
nodes.summary: Research-only minimum orientation view over local objective references, four objective statuses, bounded history, constraints, alternatives, and critical unknowns, with action/evidence/persistence authority explicitly orthogonal.
nodes.why_read: Open when reasoning about current objective, defer/supersession/completion, bounded history, blockers, ambiguity, or next-step orientation without inventing execution or persistence semantics.

research.research_question: What is the smallest bounded orientation representation needed to distinguish active objectives, history, constraints, alternatives, and unknowns without creating a goal/runtime engine?
results: four objective statuses retained: CURRENT_PRIMARY, DEFERRED, SUPERSEDED, COMPLETED
limitations: illustrative next-step terms are not a frozen enum
rejected_interpretations: reopen is a new frozen status

nodes.title: Mentaury Soul — Substrate-Neutral Projection
nodes.summary: Documentation-only projection of Soul's durable semantic distinctions across replaceable LLM, graph, database, embedding, language, and agent substrates, requiring scoped traceable revision and explicit declared loss.
nodes.why_read: Open when separating Soul semantics from a particular implementation substrate or checking whether provenance, uncertainty, revision meaning, and authority survive a future realization.

nodes.title: Mentaury Soul — Review Guide
nodes.summary: Bounded review route that starts from agent/current-state surfaces, narrows to one semantic domain, follows owning contract→implementation→tests→CI, and avoids repository-wide scanning unless focused evidence is insufficient.
nodes.why_read: Open before a Soul audit/review to keep context bounded, preserve current-vs-historical distinctions, and follow the correct owner/evidence chain.
